ResearchProjectDef.label: primitive hygiene
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build the basics of hygiene without plumbing: pit latrines, burn pits for fecal sludge, water wells for manual collection, water tubs for washing and drinking, bath mats, stall doors, and litter boxes, troughs and bowls for animals.

ResearchProjectDef.label: water supply
ResearchProjectDef.description: Supply plumbed fixtures with water: wind pumps, groundwater and surface water intakes, water butts, tanks and towers, and valves that open or close connections between pipes. Stored water must be drained if it becomes contaminated.

ResearchProjectDef.label: basic fixtures
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build basic plumbed fixtures: basins for washing hands after using the toilet, bathtubs for a comfortable, leisurely wash, and sewage outlets where sewage pools and slowly cleans up.

ResearchProjectDef.label: showers
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build showers and shower stalls that use water supplied by water towers. They can be heated via plumbed hot water tanks and do not require a sewage outlet.\n65L per wash

ResearchProjectDef.label: sinks and fountains
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build kitchen sinks that increase room cleanliness and water fountains used for drinking and washing.

ResearchProjectDef.label: large water storage
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build large stores of water for plumbed fixtures: huge water towers and, with DBH Expanded, large water tanks and large hot water tanks. Stored water must be drained if it becomes contaminated.
